detail.abstract: Mechanism design pins down only a low-dimensional projection of a function-valued contract; institutional refinements select within the residual. We establish this in a screening problem where the principal collects a contractual share of an agent’s realized cash flow and the private type is pricing ability. A reduction proposition collapses any admissible schedule to a two-dimensional sufficient statistic. An optimal-mechanism theorem delivers a closed-form trade-off: the winning agent is induced to price as a monopolist bearing his virtual cost, implementable by a menu of fixed fees and linear shares; revenue equivalence fails, and the ubiquitous flat royalty is strictly dominated. A canonical-representation theorem shows that any well-behaved refinement selects a unique contract decomposing into a mechanism-determined affine baseline plus a refinement-specific kernel correction. A separability theorem classifies refinements: robustness can be delegated—the misspecification-averse principal selects the affine baseline—whereas fairness must be co-designed with the mechanism.

title: Regime-Conditional Factor Premia and Institutional Flow Dynamics in Indian Equities

detail.title: Regime-Conditional Factor Premia and Institutional Flow Dynamics in Indian Equities
detail.abstract: We document regime-conditional factor premia in Indian equity markets and examine whether daily foreign institutional investor (FII) flows explain the underlying dynamics. Using the IIM Ahmedabad survivorship-bias-adjusted factor library (Agarwalla, Jacob, and Varma, 2013) spanning 2019–2025, we identify Bull, Sideways, and Bear market states via a Hidden Markov Model and characterise factor performance within each state. The momentum premium (WML) concentrates in Sideways regimes (Sharpe ratio 1.667, t = 3.24), while the market premium concentrates in Bull regimes (Sharpe ratio 1.485, t = 2.28). Value (HML) is directionally positive in Bear regimes (Sharpe ratio 2.26), consistent with defensive rotation into low-valuation stocks, though statistical inference is limited by the sparse Bear sample (n = 121 days). We next test whether daily NSDL FII net flows Granger-cause individual factor premia across 15 regime-factor pairs (five daily factors × three regimes), applying Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction. No cell survives — FII aggregate flows do not predict factor premia in any regime. A buy-sell decomposition reveals that gross FII volume (both purchases and sales) predicts aggregate market returns specifically in Bear regimes (F ≈ 5, p ≈ 0.009), consistent with FII acting as the marginal price setter when domestic liquidity thins; because Bear observations are concentrated in the COVID episode, this result cannot be established independently of the crisis window. Realized pairwise correlation (DCC) rises significantly in Bear (mean 0.30 vs. 0.25 in Bull; t = 22.9), confirming diversification failure coincides with regime transitions rather than leading them. A regime-aware factor allocation strategy achieves Sharpe 0.794 versus 0.733 for buy-and-hold over the 2021–2026 walk-forward period, although a static mean-variance allocation outperforms both over this sample — a result we report transparently and discuss in Section 7.

title: The Impact of Risk Management Activities on Bank Valuation
affiliations: , Villanova University - Villanova School of Business and Villanova University - Department of Finance

detail.title: The Impact of Risk Management Activities on Bank Valuation
detail.abstract: This paper examines how banks’ hedging activities influence market valuation. Using U.S. commercial bank data from 2001Q1–2024Q3, we develop a two-stage estimation process that isolates bank-specific effects on the market-to-book (MB) ratio after controlling for macroeconomic and size-related factors. We find that derivatives-based interest rate hedging is significantly and positively associated with MB, particularly during monetary tightening and for banks with high uninsured deposits, large unrealized securities losses, more liquidity creation, or greater asset-related rate sensitivity. Credit risk hedging shows no significant impact. Overall, we observe that the level of interest rate hedging activity has more than doubled during the most recent portion of our sample (2019-2024) as a greater percentage of banks began using derivatives to manage their interest rate risk. Our findings highlight market conditions and bank hedging decisions under which interest rate risk management creates shareholder value.

title: Green is the new black
affiliations: Bank of Italy and Bank of Italy

detail.title: Green is the new black
detail.abstract: Donald Trump's re-election and the renewed withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement triggered a marked deterioration in the US green bond market, reflected in both a lower probability of issuing green bonds and a contraction in issuance volumes. Moreover, the greenium -- the typically negative yield spread between green and traditional bonds with similar characteristics -- turned from negative to positive. This notable price change, coupled with reduced issuance, signals weakened investor demand for green assets, likely driven by increased uncertainty about the credibility of climate policy commitments and a less optimistic outlook for environmentally-conscious firms

title: The Geography of Incomplete Recovery: Spatial Persistence and Compound Vulnerability in United States Housing Wealth, 2007–2021

detail.title: The Geography of Incomplete Recovery: Spatial Persistence and Compound Vulnerability in United States Housing Wealth, 2007–2021

detail.abstract: Did U.S. local housing markets that suffered the deepest Great Recession losses recover during the 2020–2021 pandemic boom, or does recovery failure persist? Using IPUMS American Community Survey microdata, the FEMA National Risk Index, and Census TIGER/Line geometry, I build a real housing-wealth recovery index (2012–2021) for 2,351 PUMAs across the contiguous United States and show that recovery is strongly and durably unequal across space. It is highly clustered (Moran’s I = 0.70, p < 0.001), with 360 statistically significant Low-Low cores in the Great Lakes industrial corridor, Appalachia, and the Mississippi Delta. A k-means typology isolates a 968-PUMA “Persistently Depressed” cluster that combines the weakest recovery with the highest social vulnerability (mean SOVI = 59.6) and the lowest community resilience, a compound-disadvantage footprint that offers a regionally coherent targeting criterion for Community Reinvestment Act assessment areas. I then ask whether deeper recession losses causally shaped recovery, and find the question cannot be cleanly identified: the apparent catch-up in a naive ordinary-least-squares regression is largely a mechanical artifact of mean reversion and measurement error, and a county-level instrumental-variables design cannot resolve it, because no available instrument for recession severity is both strong and valid. The causal effect is therefore not identified in this setting, a cautionary result for the mechanical use of shift-share instruments when housing is the outcome. The paper’s robust, policy-relevant contribution is its documentation of persistent spatial inequality and compound disadvantage.

detail.abstract:
This exploratory working paper examines whether small business networks can reduce transaction costs and coordination failures through a transparent system of recorded commitments, deadlines, guarantees, and organized demand.

The paper develops a preliminary model of commitment coordination based on a reconstructed historical case from Almaty in 1998 and presents illustrative simulation results comparing fragmented exchange with auditable commitment coordination. The simulation results are model-internal and should not be interpreted as empirical validation.

The proposed pilot involves 8–12 entrepreneurs and is designed to test whether recorded obligations, visible deadlines, dispute logs, guarantor relationships, and anti-favoritism safeguards can improve coordination reliability in real small-business cooperation.

The paper outlines the model, pilot calibration plan, legal boundaries, data collection protocol, risks, success and failure metrics, and limitations.

title: The rStrings Model: Risk as a Continuous Vibrating Field: A Unifying Framework with an Extension to Unobservable Risk Dimensions

detail.title: The rStrings Model: Risk as a Continuous Vibrating Field: A Unifying Framework with an Extension to Unobservable Risk Dimensions

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest, financial or otherwise. This research received no external funding and was conducted independently. No relationships with individuals or organizations that could be perceived as influencing the results exist.

detail.abstract: Classical actuarial science models risk as a discrete event, one that either occurs or does not occur at an instant t with an assignable probability. The rStrings model, which takes from string theory its mathematical foundations: the wave equation, the decomposition into normal modes, and compactified dimensions, proposes treating risk as a continuous vibrating field extended over the coverage horizon. The model considers that the field's tension follows a diffusion process, and the claim is reinterpreted as a resonance event, the crossing of a critical threshold. The framework provides three capabilities absent from classical valuation: reserves conditioned on the observed risk trajectory, a quantifiable prevention mechanism through the reversion coefficient, and a modal decomposition of multiple coverages with a correlation hierarchy postulated from the model's geometry and empirically testable. We show that mortality tables, the Cox model, Markov chains, and stochastic intensity models are limiting cases of the framework, and we establish explicit falsifiability criteria, including a prediction with no counterpart in scalar processes. Four reproducible numerical examples illustrate standard and substandard pricing, a long-term endowment, and the modal dynamics. The present work establishes the foundations of the framework; its empirical validation is the subject of a companion paper in preparation.

title: Intelligent Environments for Urban Air Pollution Prediction in Smart Cities Leveraging Atmospheric and Traffic Data: A Multi-Deep Learning Approach

detail.title: Intelligent Environments for Urban Air Pollution Prediction in Smart Cities Leveraging Atmospheric and Traffic Data: A Multi-Deep Learning Approach
detail.abstract: Modern cities increasingly rely on heterogeneous data sources and intelligent systems to improve urban management and quality of life. Among the many dimensions of urban intelligence, air quality monitoring and prediction stand out as a critical service given the well-documented impact of atmospheric pollutants on public health. This paper presents a framework that repurposes existing traffic camera infrastructures, combined with meteorological data, to forecast pollutant concentrations without requiring extensive historical air quality records. A comparative evaluation of six deep learning architectures, namely Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Convolutional LSTM (CNNLSTM), LSTM with Attention, CNNLSTM with Attention, and Transformer, is conducted across two major Spanish cities, Madrid and Bilbao. Each architecture is evaluated over 10 independent runs with different random seeds, and statistical significance is assessed through Friedman tests followed by pairwise Wilcoxon signedrank tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction. The CNNLSTM and LSTM with Attention architectures are statistically the best-performing models overall, with no significant difference between them (mean RMSE of 5.754 and 5.672, respectively; p = 0.846). However, no single architecture dominates all scenarios: the Transformer achieves the best results for SO2, PM2.5, and PM10 in Bilbao, whereas the LSTM and LSTM with Attention form the statistically best group for O3. These findings highlight that pollutant-specific model selection, rather than a one-size-fits-all approach, is essential for operational short-term urban air quality forecasting.

title: An Analysis of Trends in the Adoption of Online Education Among Graduate Students

detail.title: An Analysis of Trends in the Adoption of Online Education Among Graduate Students
detail.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic corresponded with substantial changes in graduate-level online education in the United States. The purpose of this quantitative, non-experimental, longitudinal descriptive study was to analyze trends in exclusively online graduate enrollment before, during, and after COVID-19, and to examine whether the distribution of research doctorate completions across broad fields changed across the same periods. This study used two federal, census-level data sources: the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS) Fall Enrollment component and the Survey of Earned Doctorates (SED). Research Question 1 asked: How did the COVID-19 pandemic influence enrollment trends in online graduate education at U.S. higher education institutions? Research Question 2 asked: To what extent did the shift to online learning during the COVID-19 pandemic impact the academic performance of graduate students across different fields of study? For RQ1, an IPEDS analytic file of 15,761 institution-year observations was analyzed using a one-way ANOVA comparing exclusively online graduate enrollment (EFDEEXC) across pre-pandemic, pandemic-peak, and post-pandemic periods, supplemented by a two-way ANOVA examining the joint effects of time period and institutional control. Results indicated a statistically significant difference across periods, F(2, 15,758) = 26.62, p < .001, with a small effect (ηp² = .0034). Post-hoc comparisons showed enrollment increased significantly during the pandemic peak and remained significantly above the pre-pandemic baseline in the post-pandemic period. For Research Question 2, SED doctorate counts (2018–2022) aggregated into broad disciplinary categories were analyzed using a chi-square test of independence. The association between time period and field distribution was statistically significant, χ²(20) = 1134.25, p < .001, with a small effect (Cramer’s V = .030). Standardized residuals indicated over-representation of Engineering and Mathematics & Computer Sciences and under-representation of Humanities & Arts during and after the pandemic period. Overall, findings indicate that online graduate enrollment shifted upward after COVID-19, with post-pandemic levels remaining above the pre-pandemic baseline, while doctoral completions remained largely stable in composition with modest, field-specific variation. Implications include the need for sustained investment in online program quality, adult-learner support structures, and discipline-sensitive doctoral completion continuity planning.

detail.abstract: Social media has emerged as one of the most influential communication and marketing channels for organizations worldwide. The increasing complexity of managing multiple social media platforms has encouraged organizations to adopt social media management systems. Hootsuite is among the most widely used social media management platforms, offering content scheduling, analytics, social listening, customer engagement and collaboration capabilities. This study examines Hootsuite as a strategic social media management platform by reviewing its features, applications, pricing structure, organizational uses, benefits and limitations. Additionally, the paper evaluates real-world organizational implementations and discusses the platform's roles in improving digital marketing performance and social media governance. The findings indicate that Hootsuite significantly enhances operational efficiency, campaign management and analytical decision-making while presenting certain challenges related to cost and platform dependency. The study contributes to the growing literature on social media management systems and digital marketing technologies.

title: Ergonomic Evaluation of Knee Exoskeleton Assistance in Construction: A Multimodal Study
affiliations: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey - Rutgers University, Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey - Rutgers University, Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey - Rutgers University, Rutgers University - School of Management and Labor Relations and Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey - Rutgers University

detail.title: Ergonomic Evaluation of Knee Exoskeleton Assistance in Construction: A Multimodal Study
detail.abstract: Construction work involves physically strenuous tasks that heighten the risk of work-related musculoskeletal disorders and productivity loss. Wearable exoskeletons has shown a promising technology to help prevent work-related musculoskeletal disorders and decrease physical demands of human workers. Most existing studies evaluate wearable exoskeletons in simplified settings or isolated tasks and do not fully reflect the diverse and dynamic task demands of construction-related activities. To address this gap, this study presents an integrated framework that combines wearable knee exoskeleton assistance, immersive virtual-and augmentedreality (VR/AR) tasks, and synchronized multi-sensor data to quantify safety and performance in construction-like work space. Twenty-one adults completed multi-task protocols on a modular stair-ramp-deck platform with and without exoskeleton assistance while motion capture, force plates, electromyography, inertial sensors, and metabolic data recorded biomechanics and effort. The analyses and results indicate that exoskeleton assistance reduces lower-limb muscular demand and improves postural stability during kneeling and VR/AR tasks. Human subject survey results show perceived stability gains but note comfort and weight concerns. The evaluation framework provides a reproducible, task-relevant method for evaluating ergonomic and productivity outcomes with wearable sensing and exoskeletons in construction. The complete multimodal dataset and protocols are openly released to facilitate benchmarking and the development of future adaptive, task-aware wearable exoskeletons for workplace applications.

title: What Was Driving Part-Time Employment From 2010 Through 2019

detail.title: What Was Driving Part-Time Employment From 2010 Through 2019
detail.abstract:
During the recovery from the Great Recession and prior to the Covid Recession (2010 through 2019) the trends in Part-Time because of Slack Work or Business Conditions (PTSWBC) -- a major component of Involuntary Part-Time (IPT)-- and Voluntary Part-Time (VPT) moved in opposite directions. The sum of these two series, however, remained relatively stationary during the recovery.

Unlike previous recovery periods, this paper finds that PTSWBC and VPT were cointegrated: The two series shared a common trend. The common trend can be explained by movements in PTSWBC. Long-run movements in VPT were driven by changes in PTSWBC which had to do with employer demand for part-time work.

If the findings based on time series methods are correct, this suggest full-time positions that were converted to PTSWBC did not revert back to full-time once the recovery from the Great Recession took hold. Possible reasons could be slow moving market factors and the ACA.

Workers whose positions during the Great Recession changed from full-time to PTSWBC but did switch back would eventually vacate their part-time position. The vacated position, in turn, would be filled by a worker classified as VPT.

title: Distinctive combinations of tropical climates and soils in rainfed and irrigated agricultural areas of the tropics

detail.title: Distinctive combinations of tropical climates and soils in rainfed and irrigated agricultural areas of the tropics
detail.abstract: The tropics can be geographically defined as that part of the earth, representing the region between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn. However, the definition of the tropical region varies among scientific disciplines. The boundaries of the tropics can be defined based on surface temperature and precipitation patterns and the boundaries of the tropics can extend further from the equator than the traditional latitudinal definition. In this paper, available databases were integrated and analyzed for identifying the distinctive combinations (or occurrence within the same geographic location) of tropical climates and soils in agricultural areas of the tropical geographic region and their relations with rainfed and irrigated crops. Analyzing datasets together made it possible to highlight distinctive combinations and display their distribution in the tropical region of the world. Considering the extent in agricultural areas in the tropical region, it was concluded that Tropical Savanna Climate (Aw) is the main climate; furthermore, rainfed crops and especially irrigated crops in the tropics are mostly under this type of climate. Acrisols, Ferralsols, and Luvisols under Aw climate are the distinctive combinations for rainfed crops, and combinations of Vertisols and Luvisols with the same climate type are distinguishable for irrigated crops.

title: Why India's Air-Quality Governance Is Becoming a Template for the Global South

detail.abstract: The issue of air pollution poses one of the foremost complex governance challenges for fast-growing urban areas in the global south. This paper contends that India has positioned itself as a leading innovator in terms of air quality governance, providing a scalable and contextually relevant model for other nations in similar positions to implement. Using the lens of scholarship from environmental governance, public health and environmental justice, we analyse the new data driven-monitoring systems being developed in India, as well as the development of a new multi-level government structure to oversee the country's air quality, including through the establishment of judiciary oversight/requirements, support for transitioning the population to clean cooking solutions, transportation initiatives and consideration for co-benefits from climate action. Specifically, we highlight how many of the initiatives developed by the Government of India (i.e., the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), Bharat Stage VI fuel standards and the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, or PMUY), have helped India create stronger institutional capacity and thus improve environmental protection at the population level. The analysis of India's governance innovations demonstrates that they can provide not only a uniquely national model for implementation but also transferable lessons to other developing countries located in the global south particularly those dealing with significant resource limitations, fragmentation of institutional governance structures or severe socioeconomic inequities.

title: Adaptive Learning and Non-linear Pass-through in Small Open Economies: A Robust Machine Learning Framework for Inflation Forecasting

detail.title: Adaptive Learning and Non-linear Pass-through in Small Open Economies: A Robust Machine Learning Framework for Inflation Forecasting
detail.abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of traditional linear forecasting frameworks during periods of unprecedented supply-side anomalies. We introduce a robust macroeconomic forecasting architecture utilizing a Nested Time-Series Cross-Validation scheme to model HICP inflation in Greece (2015-2026) using exogenous global commodity indices. To eliminate the induced serial correlation inherent in overlapping filters (the Slutzky-Yule effect) and circumvent the extrapolation boundaries of tree-based ensembles, all features are transformed into first log-differences (Month-on-Month). We evaluate a regularized Machine Learning ensemble-the Random Forest Regressor-against a penalized linear baseline (Ridge Regression), optimizing all hyperparameters dynamically to eliminate tuning bias. The empirical results yield a Diebold-Mariano test statistic of 2.1909 (p-value = 0.0285). Consequently, we reject the null hypothesis of equal unconditional predictive accuracy at the 5% significance level, demonstrating the predictive superiority of the non-linear ensemble. The algorithm's ability to autonomously adjust its hierarchical complexity during the 2022 energy shock proves that adaptive tree-based architectures offer a mathematically superior approximation of inflation dynamics in volatile environments compared to globally optimized linear models. Finally, applying the optimal configuration to real-time data, the framework projects a stabilizing Month-on-Month HICP variation of-0.033% for June 2026.

detail.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic prompted significant transformations in education systems globally. Consequently, this qualitative ethnographic study aimed to analyze the evolution of attitudes among English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners through the lens of language socialization (LS). Additionally, the study explored the evolution of the COVID-19 pandemic on the LS of Iranian EFL learners within cyberspace through prolonged engagement and triangulated data collection, including classroom observations, semi-structured interviews, researcher field notes, audio recordings, and student journals. This approach allowed for a holistic understanding of the Iranian culture from participants' perspectives. A triangulation of data was collected, comprising class observations, semi-structured interviews, researcher notes, audio recordings, and student journals. The Data analysis was conducted using MAXQDA Analytic Pro 2020. Based on the seven principles of LS, the results identified eight categories: cultural familiarity, cultural differences, the influence of foreign culture, changes in identity and behavior, online class recording, online learning, self-efficacy, and participation in virtual groups. Ultimately, this study concluded that language and culture are intrinsically intertwined and that learners' engagement with language and culture adversely impacts their socialization within the English language and culture. Furthermore, online classes were found to enhance learners' self-efficacy while reducing anxiety levels. The findings equip EFL educators with strategies for fostering adaptive language socialization during crises, while offering learners tools to navigate disruptions through reflection and virtual communities. Additionally, they guide researchers in studying attitude evolution ethnographically and urge material developers to integrate psychosocial elements into language resources for volatile environments.

detail.abstract: Corporate finance theory provides two dominant frameworks for capital structure decisions: the Modigliani-Miller irrelevance proposition and the pecking order theory. Neither applies to growth-stage startups. Modigliani-Miller assumes frictionless markets and perfect information-conditions that do not exist for private, information-opaque startups. Pecking order theory predicts that firms prefer internal financing, then debt, then equity-yet venture-backed startups routinely raise equity first and debt later, precisely the opposite sequence. The result: founders navigate one of their most consequential strategic decisionswhich capital source to pursue, when, and in what amount-without a theoretically grounded or empirically validated decision framework. This paper addresses that gap. Drawing on 2024-2025 market data showing venture debt at $53.3 billion annually (up 94% from 2023), revenue-based financing emerging as a $2+ billion market, and median equity dilution at 18-20% per round, we introduce the Capital-Control-Timeline (CCT) Framework-a three-dimensional decision architecture that maps capital source choices to their trade-offs across capital efficiency (runway per dollar), control dilution (equity and governance), and timeline pressure (burn rate and milestone distance). We document four stage-specific capital strategies: Seed stage (equity-only), Series A (equity with optional RBF for working capital), Series B-C (equity with venture debt to extend runway), and Growth stage (blended equity-debt-secondary structures). We characterize conditions under which venture debt becomes theoretically optimal (post-equity raise, $2M+ ARR, clear path to next milestone), when RBF becomes theoretically viable (SaaS/e-commerce with recurring revenue, need for working capital without board interference), and when equity is theoretically necessary (pre-revenue, pivot risk, or asymmetric upside requiring patient capital). The framework is consistent with observed capital decisions across publicly-disclosed corporate cases and calibrated to 2024-2025 market conditions. For practitioners, this paper provides a structured framework for evaluating capital trade-offs that business school corporate finance courses do not teach.

detail.abstract: When the true data-generating process is Y = f(X, Z) and the working model is Y = g(X) + ε, the causal contribution of the omitted Z loads onto the residual ε, and the residual is then interpreted in the only vocabulary the model possesses. This paper names the practice of converting such residuals into measured entities-and of building policy promises on their removal-the residual fallacy, formalizes it, and develops operational criteria for detecting and preventing it. The lead case is the Canadian internal-trade-barrier literature, 2016-2026, which supplies an unusually complete audit trail: the "barrier" is the residual of a regression on an inference; the canonical source records, in its own footnotes, negative barriers, missing data priced as a barrier, and non-tradability booked as policy; the projected gain is arithmetic in an assumed elasticity, positive by construction in the model class employed; and across published vintages the entity's measured size halved (from a 21 percent to a roughly 9 percent tariff equivalent) while the gain promised from its removal nearly doubled (from roughly 4 to roughly 7 percent of GDP), with no statute repealed and no tariff discovered in the interim. The mirror-image fallacy-discarding a measured relationship for want of a mechanism-is documented through the loss of the scurvy cure and the rejection of Semmelweis. Five operational tests are proposed, together with the single question underlying all of them: is the model's premise-set certified complete, or merely assumed so?

detail.abstract: The distributional incidence of monetary policy is usually treated as an empirical question, answered after the fact from administrative microdata. This paper shows it is an arithmetic question, answerable in advance. Banks operate the standard amortization formula in inverted form-payment capacity in, maximum loan out-and the resulting function P_max(r) is convex and steepest near zero. Composed with the creditworthiness spread schedule, which prices each borrower's buffer and is itself codified in Basel supervisory doctrine, and with the power-law distribution of wealth, the incidence of any uniform rate cut is structurally regressive by closedform calculation, before any asset price moves. A feedback corollary follows: rate cuts enlarge buffers, buffers compress spreads, and the next cut amplifies from a steeper distribution, making the wealth distribution partly the instrument's own output. The March 2020 cuts in five owncurrency countries supply a natural experiment: with borders closed and incomes collapsing, every competing explanation of house prices predicted the wrong sign. Applied to Canada, the arithmetic yields gains on the order of $188 million per household at the apex of the distribution against roughly $37,000 across the bottom 80 percent, an aggregate stimulus approximately 7.2 times the fiscal response-computable in advance from public data and the banks' own formula.

detail.abstract: A recent study explored how scholars in the digital humanities research domain are navigating this new and complex landscape. Digital humanities is an interdisciplinary research field where scholars employ digital tools and computational methods to investigate cultural and humanities questions. Drawing on an international survey of 76 respondents and 15 in-depth interviews, the study found that scholars are not simply embracing or rejecting these tools. Instead, they are adopting AI systems cautiously, using them to speed up routine tasks, explore ideas, and build new skills, while navigating problems of accuracy, authorship, and what these systems might mean for the future of scholarship. The big question is no longer just whether AI is impressive, but whether it is becoming a genuine research partner, a useful tool, or, for some, still more of a “dancing bear” than a trusted collaborator. By tracing these mixed reactions and everyday practices, the study offers a grounded look at how AI is beginning to reshape academic life.

detail.title: The Impact Frontier
detail.abstract: How much can a marginal portfolio tilt by an investor change firms’ capital and the external outcomes those firms produce? This paper develops a general-equilibrium model in which investor capital supply and firm capital demand jointly determine the real effects of sustained portfolio tilts. The model nests the CAPM, incorporates investor heterogeneity through a non-market-risk term, and aligns firm capital demand with q-theory. The resulting Impact Frontier is the Pareto frontier between certainty-equivalent financial returns and portfolio impact returns. The direct contribution multiplier is the share of an investor’s supply shift that becomes firm capital in the one-asset case; for multiple assets, a contribution multiplier matrix maps portfolio tilts into capital changes across firms. Calibrated to U.S. public equities with five-year return and capital-growth windows, the estimated multipliers vary substantially across firms. Tilts that ignore contribution-multiplier heterogeneity can fall far below the Impact Frontier or move in the wrong direction. Direct-multiplier tilts capture most of the frontier for the full cross-section, while the full matrix matters more within narrower investment universes.

detail.abstract: Information security has become a critical organizational priority as businesses increasingly depend on digital technologies to support operations, decision-making, and service delivery. This paper examines the role of information security in strengthening organizational performance and supporting digital transformation through a case analysis of D. Reyes Pharmacy, a community-based healthcare enterprise in San Agustin, Isabela. The study identifies key operational challenges, including fragmented processes, disconnected systems, limited data visibility, and potential security vulnerabilities resulting from the use of manual and standalone information management practices. Using a case study and organizational assessment approach, the paper proposes the implementation of an Integrated Pharmacy Information System (PIS) supported by security controls such as role-based access management, user authentication, data encryption, audit trails, and automated backup mechanisms. Findings suggest that integrating information security into business processes can improve data accuracy, operational efficiency, governance, risk management, and decision-making capabilities while enhancing stakeholder trust and business continuity. To support implementation, a phased policy framework is presented that aligns system development, organizational change management, employee capability development, and continuous quality improvement initiatives. The paper argues that information security should be viewed not merely as a technical function but as a strategic business capability that contributes to organizational resilience, competitiveness, and sustainable growth. The proposed framework offers practical guidance for small and medium-sized healthcare organizations seeking to strengthen information security while advancing digital transformation objectives.

title: Norm-induced Self-censorship in a behavioral Model of Online Communication

detail.title: Norm-induced Self-censorship in a behavioral Model of Online Communication

detail.abstract: This paper develops a behavioral game-theoretic model of online communication in which the quality and visibility of information are jointly determined by sender incentives, audience reactions, and platform design. Senders are either truth-seeking or popularity-seeking. They choose how much to verify a message and how evocative to make it before sharing. Receivers form beliefs about the message, react through likes or dislikes, or choose not to react. These reactions are shaped by endogenous approval and condemnation norms, and sender types evolve through replicator dynamics. The model shows that engagement incentives can reward evocative but weakly veried content. It also identies a mechanism of norm-induced self-censorship: truth-seeking agents may remain silent when expected disapproval is suciently strong, so accurate information can exist without being expressed. Analytical results characterize receiver-equilibrium uniqueness, the silence threshold, and the existence of interior evolutionary equilibria. Numerical results show that stronger social feedback does not necessarily improve the informational environment. Condemnation norms can expand self-censorship, approval norms can partly oset it, and the eect of overall norm intensity on truthful expression can be non-monotonic. The paper also studies platform friction as an intervention. Friction reduces realized exposure and weakens the advantage of attention-seeking communication. When combined with learning, it can also increase the value of verication and improve the quality of information that is actually read. The contribution of the paper is to provide a tractable framework linking verication, evocativeness, norm-based audience reactions, evolutionary selection, and platform intervention.

title: The Digital Welfare of Nations: New Measures of Welfare Gains and Inequality
affiliations: National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER), Carnegie Mellon University, Meta, Meta, Meta, Meta Platforms Inc and Northwestern University

detail.title: The Digital Welfare of Nations: New Measures of Welfare Gains and Inequality
detail.abstract: Digital goods can generate large benefits for consumers, but these benefits are largely unmeasured in the national accounts, including GDP and productivity. In this paper, we measure welfare gains from 10 popular digital goods across 13 countries by conducting large-scale incentivized online choice experiments on representative samples of nearly 40,000 people. We estimate that these goods-many of which are free to users-generate on the order of $2.5 trillion in aggregate consumer welfare across these countries per year, which is roughly equivalent to 6% of their combined GDP. These aggregate figures are estimated with less precision than standard national accounts measures and should be interpreted as order-of-magnitude rather than point estimates. We find that lower-income individuals and lower-income countries obtain relatively larger welfare gains from these goods compared to higher-income individuals and countries. This suggests that digital goods may reduce inequality in welfare within and across countries by disproportionately benefiting lower-income groups.

detail.abstract: Organisations have always operated under conditions of bounded rationality and imperfect information (Simon, 1947; March & Simon, 1958), and management control systems emerged as mechanisms to support decision-making under such conditions (Simons, 1995). What appears to be new, however, is that the incompleteness of information itself is gradually becoming traceable and governable through digital data architectures (Abraham et al., 2019; W3C, 2013). Against this background, this study pursues a rather simple question: how can companies build data systems that make ESG performance not only reportable, but also steerable? By this, I mean data that can be verified in real time, used within ordinary controlling cycles, and traced from a single sensor on the shop floor through to a KPI on a board-level slide. This paper is based on a qualitative case study of a retrofit IoT architecture (the Modbus Cloud Connect) developed within grandcentrix, an IoT subsidiary of the Vodafone Group. From this case study it derives the conceptual idea of the Green (Retrofit) Digital Twin (GRDT), a controlling-oriented architecture that connects existing operational systems to audit-ready ESG data without requiring a replacement of the underlying infrastructure. These relationships are summarised in the conceptual framework T × G × C → I (Technology × Governance × Controlling → Impact), the central idea of which is that impact collapses once governance fails, even when the underlying technology is highly advanced. The contribution is therefore positioned less as a study of sustainability reporting requirements, and more as a management control paper concerned with what happens once ESG data are treated with the same care that has long been afforded to financial data. From this case, six design principles are derived, which are then examined against a second case (ALMiG Kompressoren GmbH, 2022). Taken together, they describe a vendor-neutral path leading from a single meter through to an ESRS-aligned KPI and thereby offer a practical point of departure for companies seeking to build robust controlling structures around their sustainability data.

The evidence supports the need for auditable indicators and effective data-access obligations under the DSA and the EU AI Act.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Schmalenbach Journal of Business Research, volume 78, issue 3, 2026[10.1007/s41471-026-00239-8]

detail.abstract: Using the coronavirus pandemic (COVID-19) as a natural experiment, recent studies have shown that digitalization has been key for improved firm performance. While earlier studies mostly use the canonical binary difference-indifference design, recent advances have shown that this may lead to biased results when the digitalization treatment variable is continuous (treatment heterogeneity). In this paper we show that digitalization, measured in terms of online sales, has indeed been a significant driver of firm performance during the coronavirus pandemic (COVID-19) also when considering treatment heterogeneity. Using World Bank Enterprise Surveys data for ten Western European countries shows that initially fully digitalized firms with 100% of sales online experienced 10%-point higher firm-level sales growth during the pandemic when average firm sales contracted by 8.7%. Our results are robust to controlling for unobserved and observed firm heterogeneity, treatment heterogeneity and sample selectivity, while the common trend assumption is validated and further robustness is confirmed using a placebo test. This study contributes to the literature by providing a rigorous estimate of the importance of digitalization for firm performance within the context of a natural experiment.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Organizational Openness, and Dynamic Capabilities: Tensions and Limits in the Reconfiguration of Established Firms
affiliations: and FGV EAESP - Sao Paulo School of Business Administration

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence, Organizational Openness, and Dynamic Capabilities: Tensions and Limits in the Reconfiguration of Established Firms

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Fundação Getulio Vargas (FGV EAESP). All participants provided informed consent prior to participation. Interviews were conducted voluntarily, recorded with permission, and anonymized during analysis. The study complied with applicable ethical standards for research involving human participants.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly expanding firms' exposure to external knowledge, partners, and digital ecosystems, yet greater openness has not produced uniform competitive transformation. This paper asks how AI-mediated organizational openness reshapes internal routines and capability reconfiguration in established firms, and why similar levels of openness lead to divergent outcomes. Building on the microfoundations of dynamic capabilities, sensing, seizing, and transforming (Teece, 2007), we conducted a qualitative multi-case study with abductive logic, based on seven in-depth interviews with senior executives from six established Brazilian firms across five sectors. Primary data were triangulated with publicly available institutional documents, and analysis followed the Gioia methodology, producing a three-level data structure from which seven central analytical patterns were constructed. The results reveal a paradox of AI-mediated openness: exposure expands, but internal reconfiguration does not necessarily follow. Specifically: (i) a systemic tension between amplified sensing and constrained seizing operates in six of seven cases, the seizing bottleneck is human, cultural, and political, not informational; (ii) firms display radical heterogeneity in openness architectures, organized into four maturity profiles; (iii) organizational culture functions as an active microfoundation of seizing, constituting an institutional barrier that AI cannot overcome regardless of its technical maturity; (iv) AI amplifies sensing but does not resolve the seizing bottleneck in any case studied; (v) transforming is asymmetric and conditioned by the effectiveness of the sensing-seizing chain; (vi) AI does not function as a mechanism of openness, it operates inside firm boundaries, not at the edge of the ecosystem; and (vii) AI governance is universally incipient, with no firm possessing a dedicated governance body, and all conflating data protection with AI governance. As a theoretical contribution, the study integrates organizational openness, dynamic capabilities, and artificial intelligence in a unified empirical analysis, demonstrating that AI is a necessary but insufficient condition for capability reconfiguration, and that artificial intelligence acts not as a structural transformer but as an amplifier of existing capability configurations. As a practical contribution, a four-profile typology offers a diagnostic instrument for managers seeking to identify their current position and next strategic moves in terms of openness and AI adoption.

Governing the Convergence: Artificial Intelligence, Quantum Computing,
and the Future of India's Legal-Digital Order

keywords: AI and convergence of Qunatum COmputing

detail.abstract:
India stands at a consequential juncture in its legal-digital order. Artificial intelligence is no longer a prospective technology - it is operationally embedded across healthcare diagnostics, judicial support infrastructure, financial services, law enforcement, and public welfare delivery. Simultaneously, expert consensus places the arrival of cryptographically relevant quantum computers, capable of breaking the RSA and elliptic-curve encryption securing Aadhaar, UPI, inter-bank settlement systems, and digital legal records, within the 2028-2033 window. These two trajectories are not parallel developments to be governed in isolation. Their convergence creates compounded risks that India's current regulatory architecture - the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023, the Information Technology Act 2000, and the proposed Digital India Act - is structurally unprepared to address.

This policy brief maps AI deployment across six sectors in India, identifies provisions of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act that India's constitutional and administrative context can productively accommodate, and analyses those that cannot be transplanted wholesale into a developing-country framework characterised by state-led AI deployment, limited institutional capacity, and a distinct fundamental rights architecture anchored in K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India and PUCL v. Union of India. The quantum computing dimension is treated not as a future contingency but as a present-tense risk already shaping adversarial harvest-now-decrypt-later behaviour targeting sensitive state and financial data. A dimension absent from existing Indian policy literature is also examined: Software Bills of Materials as a foundational layer of AI supply chain transparency and a necessary precondition for effective post-quantum cryptographic migration, now mandated under CERT-In Guidelines v2.0 and SEBI's Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework. Five actionable policy recommendations are advanced, two of which require no primary legislation and can be initiated within the current administrative year. The brief is addressed to MeitY, NITI Aayog, the Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy, and the Centre for Internet and Society.

title: Optimal Medical Liability for AI
affiliations: Harvard University

detail.title: Optimal Medical Liability for AI

publicationDetails.journalName: NBER Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
I study medical liability when artificial intelligence acts as a doctor rather than as a passive clinical tool. The central object is the legally usable medical record: the inputs, logs, warnings, prescriptions, follow-up instructions, and outcomes on which courts, contracts, insurers, and regulators can condition responsibility. I show that AI medical liability is an institutional design problem under imperfect legal information. If the record separates AI-controllable error from patient nonadherence and natural disease progression, high-powered AI-fault liability implements the standard accident-law ideal. If the record is coarse, the first best may be infeasible: the same transfer that disciplines the AI also insures the patient's hidden action. With joint causation, the relevant object is a marginal-responsibility score rather than a posterior cause label. I characterize the feasible set of liability incentives generated by the record and show when the optimal rule is no liability, strict liability, negligence, a safe harbor, comparative fault, or a continuous warranty. I then study algorithmic defensive design, through which AI developers can design not only medical recommendations but also the record on which future liability depends. Adoption, learning, enterprise liability, insurance, no-fault compensation, and regulation enter as ways to change the record, the liable entity, or the financing of compensation. The framework yields conditional implications rather than a one-size-fits-all rule.

title: Can Online Activity Be Regulated? Evidence from Adult Websites

The consequences of online regulations depend on the extent to which users can circumvent restrictions or substitute toward noncompliant platforms. Since 2023, 25 U.S. states have implemented age verification laws that caused prominent adult websites (including Pornhub) to restrict local access for all users. We study how these restrictions affected browsing activity using individual-level panel data. Access restrictions reduced overall time spent on adult sites by roughly 10%. Specifically, for every 100 hours spent on top adult sites before restrictions, about 50 hours remained accessible at noncompliant sites that never restricted access, 30 hours persisted through VPN-based circumvention, 10 hours were substituted from compliant sites to noncompliant sites, and 10 hours were no longer spent on adult sites.

detail.title: FDI, gravity, and aggregation: revisiting the distance elasticity with sector-level FDI data

publicationDetails.journalName: ECB: Working Paper Series (Topic)

detail.abstract: This paper re-examines foreign direct investment motives in the ‘FDI gravity’ model (Kleinert and Toubal, 2010), focusing on the role of distance. More precisely, we investigate whether aggregate and pooled gravity models for FDI obscure relevant heterogeneities across sectors. This is possible through the novel MREID dataset, which provides us with FDI data at the 2-digit NAICS level for 184 countries over the period 2010 to 2020. Our results reveal that aggregate and pooled models mask significant sector heterogeneities in two aspects: (i) in the importance of horizontal versus vertical FDI motives, and (ii) in the distance elasticity. Distance is negatively correlated with FDI on an aggregate level, which is robust to multiple econometric specifications, but exhibits significant sector heterogeneity. Our analysis suggests the presence of complex sector-specific components that cannot easily be explained with standard economic rationales.
